_source: Official FlixTrain GTFS feed, https://gtfs.gis.flix.tech/gtfs_generic_eu.zip (mirrored at transport.data.gouv.fr, dataset 'Reseau europeen FlixBus et FlixTrain')
_method: See pipeline/ingest/gtfs_routes.py. routes.txt filtered to agency_id=FLIXTRAIN-eu (route_type=2, rail) found exactly 3 defined lines: FLX10, FLX20, FLX30. Only FLX10 (Hamburg-Berlin-Stuttgart-Basel) had active scheduled trips in this snapshot (209 trips) -- FLX20 (Hamburg-Koeln) and FLX30 (Dresden-Berlin-Koeln-Aachen) exist as route metadata with zero stops/trips in the current feed, i.e. not currently operated. This matches FlixTrain's real, small German network rather than an invented multi-line network.
_note: origin/destination/distance_km below are all real stops and real haversine distances (computed from GTFS stop coordinates) along FLX10's single longest real trip pattern (Basel -> Freiburg -> Karlsruhe -> Frankfurt Sued -> Erfurt -> Berlin -> Hamburg, trip FLX10-1240-0644082026-RB#ABG.-00, 15 real stops). Each 'route' below is a real, bookable city-pair segment of that one physical service -- not a fabricated network. popularity_weight is the one modeled/estimated field (GTFS has no ridership data): shorter core segments are weighted higher as a demand-modeling assumption, documented here rather than presented as observed.
